claim: Bock Casemates are part of a 23 km underground tunnel system carved into the rock for defensive purposes and are UNESCO-listed.
quote: As part of an original system of underground galleries and tunnels stretching over 23 km, built into the rock for defensive purposes, the Bock Casemates bear witness to the former importance of the fortress of Luxembourg.

claim: Bock Casemates open March 1 to November 2, 10:00-17:00 (18:00 in summer), adult tickets €8.
quote: The Bock Casemates opening hours for 2026 are open March 1 - November 2, 10:00-17:00 (18:00 in summer). Adult tickets cost 8 EUR.

claim: Chemin de la Corniche is a 17th-century rampart promenade dubbed 'the most beautiful balcony of Europe' by Luxembourg writer Batty Weber, running from the Bock to the Holy Ghost Citadel.
quote: Chemin de la Corniche runs along the Alzette valley on the ramparts built by the Spaniards and the French in the 17th century, from the Bock Promontory up to the lower part of the Holy Ghost Citadel, called "Rondellen". It's called "the most beautiful balcony of Europe" according to the Luxembourg writer Batty Weber.

claim: The 1.1 km Corniche promenade gives views over the Alzette gorge toward the Wenceslas Wall and lower town of Grund.
quote: The 1.1 km promenade offers jaw-dropping views over the Alzette River and the lower town of Grund. This pedestrian promenade winds along the course of the 17th-century city ramparts with views across the river canyon towards the hefty fortifications of the Wenzelsmauer (Wenceslas Wall).

claim: A circular city walk descends through the Grund and Clausen former brewery districts and follows the Pétrusse stream to its confluence with the Alzette.
quote: discover the beauties of the city with its former brewery districts Grund and Clausen, going down into the Pétrusse Valley and following the stream to its mouth into the Alzette River.

claim: The Pétrusse Casemates reopened after major works with new lighting scenography; 45-minute tours, entrance at Place de la Constitution, open daily.
quote: After extensive enhancement and security works, the Pétrusse Casemates reopened with a cutting-edge scenography and mesmerising light installations that bring history to life.

claim: Place d'Armes, created in 1671, is the central square nicknamed the 'Parlor of the City' and hosts cafés, summer bandstand concerts, a second/fourth-Saturday flea market and the Winterlights Christmas market.
quote: Place d'Armes is Luxembourg's most popular and central square, created in 1671. Nicknamed the "Parlor of the City," this square dates back to the 17th century.

claim: Grand Ducal Palace guided tours run 18 July to 30 August 2026, last 1h15, cover the Grand Duke's office, dining room and Salon des Rois, and are offered in FR/EN/DE/LB; no photos inside.
quote: In 2026, guided tours of the Palace will take place from 18 July to 30 August inclusive. The guided tour lasts 1h15. On this 75-minute tour, visitors can take a look behind the scenes, including the Grand Duke's office, the dining room and the "Salon des Rois".

claim: Notre-Dame Cathedral was built 1613–1621 by Jesuits, is free to enter, and its crypt holds the tomb of John the Blind, King of Bohemia, plus deceased Grand Ducal family members.
quote: The cathedral "Notre-Dame" of Luxembourg was built between 1613 and 1621 by the Jesuits to serve as a church to their college. The crypt is the resting place of John the Blind, King of Bohemia and Count of Luxembourg, as well as deceased members of the Grand Ducal family.

claim: Mudam's 2026 lineup includes Igshaan Adams (10.02–16.08.2026), Simon Fujiwara 'A Whole New World' (20.03–23.08.2026), Superflex 'The Bank' (15.05–30.09.2026), 'Dodeka, 12 Works for 12 Cantons' (16.05–04.10.2026) and Christine Sun Kim from 25.09.2026.
quote: Igshaan Adams: Between Then and Now 10.02 – 16.08.2026; Simon Fujiwara: A Whole New World 20.03 – 23.08.2026; Superflex: The Bank 15.05 – 30.09.2026; Dodeka, 12 Works for 12 Cantons 16.05 – 04.10.2026

claim: Mudam is closed Tuesdays; open Mon and Thu-Sun 10-18, Wed 10-21; adult entry €8 (€5 under 26).
quote: Monday: 10h00 – 18h00; Closed on Tuesday; Wednesday: 10h00 – 21h00; Thursday – Sunday: 10h00 – 18h00. Entrance fees are 8€ for adults, and 5€ for visitors under 26 years old and groups.

claim: The Nationalmusée (MNHA) is closed Mondays; open Tue-Wed and Fri-Sun 10-18 and Thu 10-20, with free admission to permanent collections.
quote: Monday - Closed, Tuesday-Wednesday - 10:00-18:00, Thursday - 10:00-20:00, Friday-Sunday - 10:00-18:00. The permanent exhibitions at the National Museum of History and Art Luxembourg are free to enter.

claim: MNHA is presenting the temporary exhibition 'Drama and Tenderness – Flemish, Spanish and Italian Art of the Baroque'.
quote: The National Museum of History and Art (MNHA) is honoured to present the exhibition Drama and Tenderness - Flemish, Spanish and Italian Art of the Baroque.

claim: The Lëtzebuerg City Museum's permanent exhibition 'The Luxembourg Story' fills 2,200 m² over three lower levels and tells the city's history from the 10th century to today, with upper floors for temporary shows.
quote: The Lëtzebuerg City Museum presents its permanent exhibition "The Luxembourg Story" on the three lower levels of the museum as well as in a space devoted to current town planning (2,200 m² in total), telling the eventful history of the city of Luxembourg from its origins in the 10th century to the present day.

claim: The Philharmonie's 2025/26 season celebrates György Kurtág's 100th birthday and features Renaud Capuçon as Artist in Focus.
quote: The 2025/26 season celebrates György Kurtág's 100th birthday in 2026. French violinist Renaud Capuçon returns as Artist in focus at the Philharmonie this season.

claim: The Philharmonie at Place de l'Europe on Kirchberg has three halls (1,500/313/180 seats) and specialises in classical music.
quote: The Philharmonie Luxembourg is located at Place de l'Europe in the Kirchberg quarter. The venue has three concert halls with capacities of 1,500, 313, and 180 places, specializing in classical music.

claim: Since 29 February 2020 all buses, trams and 2nd-class trains in Luxembourg are free for residents and tourists; only 1st class and cross-border services still require tickets.
quote: Since February 29, 2020, public transport has been free for everybody, including tourists, covering trains, trams and buses. The only exception is tickets and subscriptions for 1st class.

claim: Vel'OH! provides nearly 1,000 electric pedal-assist shared bikes across 100+ stations in Luxembourg City with a 30–40 km range and contactless bank-card unlock.
quote: There are 100+ stations in Luxembourg City and the surrounding area, and the system provides access to nearly 1,000 shared bikes. All the bikes have an electric pedal-assist system, with a range of 30–40 km. The new bikes have additional features: the multi-function handlebars let you take the bike out of the dock using your contactless bank card.

claim: Mudam was designed by Pritzker-winning architect I. M. Pei and built on the site of Fort Thüngen on the Kirchberg plateau, near the EU institutions.
quote: The building was designed by Pritzker Prize-winning architect I. M. Pei, and cost $100m to build. The museum stands on the site of the old Fort Thüngen, on the southwestern edge of the Kirchberg-plateau.
